passages.text: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard about Hezekiah’s illness and recovery.
passages.sermon:
Merodach-baladan was the king of Babylon.
He was the son of Baladan.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah had been very sick.
Hezekiah recovered from his illness.
Merodach-baladan heard that Hezekiah was sick and then recovered.
At that time, Merodach-baladan sent letters to Hezekiah.
He also sent a gift to Hezekiah.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֡וא שָׁלַ֡ח מְרֹדַ֣ךְ בַּ֠לְאֲדָן בֶּֽן־ בַּלְאֲדָ֧ן מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֛ל סְפָרִ֥ים וּמִנְחָ֖ה אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ וַיִּשְׁמַ֕ע כִּ֥י חָלָ֖ה וַֽיֶּחֱזָֽק׃

passages.text: And Hezekiah welcomed the envoys gladly and showed them what was in his treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, as well as his entire armory—all that was found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah welcomed the envoys from Babylon with joy.
Hezekiah showed the envoys his treasure house.
He showed them the silver.
He showed them the gold.
He showed them the spices.
He showed them the precious oil.
He showed them his entire armory.
He showed them everything found in his storehouses.
Hezekiah did not hide anything in his palace from the envoys.
Hezekiah showed them everything in all his dominion.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂמַ֣ח עֲלֵיהֶם֮ חִזְקִיָּהוּ֒ וַיַּרְאֵ֣ם אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית נְכֹתָה אֶת־ הַכֶּסֶף֩ וְאֶת־ הַזָּהָ֨ב וְאֶת־ הַבְּשָׂמִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת׀ הַשֶּׁ֣מֶן הַטּ֗וֹב וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִמְצָ֖א בְּאֹֽצְרֹתָ֑יו לֹֽא־ הָיָ֣ה דָבָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־ הֶרְאָ֧ם חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּבֵית֖וֹ וּבְכָל־ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah and asked, “Where did those men come from, and what did they say to you?” “They came to me from a distant land,” Hezekiah replied, “from Babylon.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
He went to King Hezekiah.
Isaiah spoke to Hezekiah.
Isaiah asked, “What did those men say?”
Isaiah also asked, “Where did they come from?”
Hezekiah answered Isaiah.
Hezekiah said, “They came to me from a distant land.”
Hezekiah said, “They came from Babylon.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו מָ֥ה אָמְר֣וּ׀ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וּמֵאַ֙יִן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ מֵאֶ֧רֶץ רְחוֹקָ֛ה בָּ֥אוּ אֵלַ֖י מִבָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: “What have they seen in your palace?” Isaiah asked. “They have seen everything in my palace,” answered Hezekiah. “There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
He spoke to King Hezekiah.
Isaiah asked Hezekiah a question.
Isaiah said, “What did the men see in your palace?”
Hezekiah answered Isaiah.
Hezekiah said, “They saw everything in my palace.”
Hezekiah said, “I showed them all my treasures.”
Hezekiah said, “There is nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֥ה רָא֖וּ בְּבֵיתֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ אֵ֣ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּבֵיתִי֙ רָא֔וּ לֹֽא־ הָיָ֥ה דָבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ הִרְאִיתִ֖ים בְּאוֹצְרֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD of Hosts: The time will surely come when everything in your palace and all that your fathers have stored up until this day will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
He spoke to King Hezekiah.
Isaiah said, “Hear the word of the LORD of Hosts.”
The LORD of Hosts is the God who commands all the armies of heaven.
Isaiah said, “Days are coming.”
In those days, everything in your palace will be taken away.
All the treasures your ancestors stored up until today will be taken away.
They will be carried off to Babylon.
Nothing will remain.
The LORD has spoken this.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ הִנֵּה֮ יָמִ֣ים בָּאִים֒ וְנִשָּׂ֣א׀ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵיתֶ֗ךָ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר אָצְר֧וּ אֲבֹתֶ֛יךָ עַד־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה בָּבֶ֑ל לֹֽא־ יִוָּתֵ֥ר דָּבָ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah spoke to King Hezekiah.
Isaiah gave a message from the LORD.
Isaiah said some of Hezekiah’s descendants will be taken away.
These descendants will be Hezekiah’s own children and grandchildren.
Enemies will take them from their homeland.
They will become eunuchs.
They will serve in the palace of the king of Babylon.
passages.original: וּמִבָּנֶ֜יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵצְא֧וּ מִמְּךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תּוֹלִ֖יד יִקָּ֑חוּ וְהָיוּ֙ סָרִיסִ֔ים בְּהֵיכַ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: But Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “At least there will be peace and security in my lifetime.”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Isaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Hezekiah spoke to Isaiah.
Hezekiah said, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good.”
Hezekiah thought about his own life.
Hezekiah said, “There will be peace and truth in my days.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶֽל־ יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ ט֥וֹב דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י יִהְיֶ֛ה שָׁל֥וֹם וֶאֱמֶ֖ת בְּיָמָֽי׃פ
